substeps.caption: The other way: no plug at all. Tray A's line runs from an e-spool on the rear wall (igus: power, data and air on one spool, no slip ring, up to 15 m), along the 30 mm between the tray's side and the extractor's guide rails.
Out of the slot: the line pays out as the extractor pulls the tray.

The catch: while tray A is out, its line spans the shaft at the extractor's height, so the extractor can't move to fetch any other tray until tray A goes home.
So a tether suits one tray, stored at the opening's own height so it never moves up or down. From the top slot here (R4, 2700 mm) it would need 2.8 m and cross the shaft on the slant.
